title: Etienne Bourdeaux to Maarten van der Goes, Berlin, 31 January 1801 (DECODE R1944)

steps.what: Retrieved the two R1944 scans: cipher groups only, with closing and signature.
Viewed the neighbouring records R1945 and R1946; R1946 image 3 is a clear sheet headed N. 16, Berlyn 31 January 1801, (get.) Bourdeaux.
Re-read the scan (corrected renvoy, positiever); checked consecutive folio stamps 294/295 and that ~90 words fit ~110 code groups.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the contemporary clear copy and its translation, copied from NOTES.md to texts/; the ~110 code groups were never transcribed (project work)

outcome.method_basis: The ministry's contemporary clear copy of the despatch (fol. 295, N. 16, Berlin 31 Jan 1801) was found misfiled as image 3 of DECODE R1946 and transcribed; the code groups were not decoded.
outcome.notes: Plaintext from the contemporary clear copy; the code was not decoded group by group.

credits.note: ministry's clear copy (fol. 295, N. 16), misfiled as image 3 of DECODE R1946

texts.label: R1944, Etienne Bourdeaux, Berlin, 31 Jan 1801 (clear copy, no. 16)
texts.summary: The Dutch chargé d'affaires in Berlin reports that Rosenkrantz does not know why he was dismissed and supposes his cipher was taken and copied by a servant; Lusi says more definitely that the desk holding his cipher was forced open, which is why Schuer was to be sent to Petersburg with a new cipher. So the letter, itself in cipher, reports a compromised codebook.

prior.where: The ministry's clear copy, fol. 295, misfiled under DECODE R1946.

human: Supplied authenticated DECODE access and posed the target.
